artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for all 5 phases: rule, advisory hook, six-agent reinforcement, doc-policy clause, end-to-end validation

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented all four task-number-leakage enforcement layers: a new auto-applied rule, an advisory PostToolUse hook hand-verified as wired into settings.json, MUST NOT reinforcement clauses in all six implementation agents, and a documentation-policy clause mirrored across both canonical and deployed copies. End-to-end validation confirmed the regex (10/10 positives, 0/13 negatives), hook wiring, agent coverage, and byte-identical doc copies.

memory_candidates.content: When an agent-file target under .claude/agents/ is actually a symlink to .claude/extensions/{ext}/agents/*.md (as with cslib-implementation-agent.md and cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md), the Edit tool refuses to write through the symlink -- resolve it first with `readlink -f` and edit the real target file directly. Also remember `grep -r` does not follow symlinks by default, so a `grep -rl <pattern> .claude/agents/` coverage check will silently omit symlinked agent files; verify those separately with a direct `grep -l <pattern> <symlink-path>` (which does follow through to the target) or `grep -rL`.

For a hook that must reference the very pattern it forbids (e.g. an anti-task-number-citation rule whose own rule text needs to give a 'before' example of a task-number citation), phrase the illustrative example inside a markdown code fence under a 'Before'/'Bad example' label using letter-only placeholders ("task N", "tasks N-M") rather than a real digit-bearing citation in prose -- this satisfies both the dogfooding constraint (the rule file itself must not read as a real citation) and keeps the regex-based advisory hook from mis-firing outside its intended illustrative-example fencing.
